Mr Md. Asaduzzaman, Advocate with Mr Shah Muhammad Ezaz Rahman, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record -------- For the Appellants. 
Mr Abut Kalam Chowdhury, Advocate instructed by Mr Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No. 1.

parties:
Fazlur Rahman being dead his heirs and successors: Md. Firozur Rahman and others ----- Appellants
-Vs-
Most Nasima Banu and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 9th day of February, 2010 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2083 of 2003)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated the 9th day of February, 2010 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2083 of 2003 discharging the Rule. 

2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the predecessor of the appellants instituted Miscellaneous Case No.87 of 1978 in the Court of Munsif, Sadar, Rajshahi for pre-emption of the case land under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 stating, inter alia, that one Nasimon Nessa Bibi was the original owner and C.S. tenant of the case land, who died as a widow and issueless leaving behind her only brother Sadar Mollah as her sole heir. Sadar Mollah died leaving behind two sons, namely, Baziur Rahman and Fazlur Rahman and two daughters named Mazeda and Salma. Thereafter, Mazeda died leaving behind her husband, two sons and one daughter. Thereafter, husband of Mazeda died leaving behind his four sons and five daughters. Salma died unmarried leaving behind her two step brothers, namely, Bazlur Rahman and Fazlur Rahman. Thus, Bazlur Rahman and Fazlur Rahman became co-sharers by inheritance in the case land. Bazlur Rahman died leaving behind the opposite party Nos.2-8 who sold their share on 12.06.1975 to the pre-emptee No. 1 through present case kabala. After knowing about such transfer, the pre-emptor, Fazlur Rahman filed Pre-emption Case No.113 of 1975 before registration of the kabala under section 60 of the Registration Act, 1908. The kabala was registered on 17.12.1977 and, there-after, the pre-emptor withdrew the said pre-emption case with the leave of the Court on the ground that the said pre-emption case was premature. After obtaining certified copy of the kabala on 03.02.1978, the pre-emptor, Fazlur Rahman, again filed Pre-emption Case No.87 of 1978 stating that the purchaser pre-emptee is a stranger in the case land and he(pre-emptor) has right to pre-empt the case land under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 as co-sharer by inheritance in the case land. The S.A. and R.S. records were duly prepared in the names of said Bazlur Rahman and Fazlur Rahman. 

3. Pre-emptee No.1 contested the case by filing a written objection denying the material allegations of the pre-emptor contending, inter alia, that before the transfer of the case land, notice was duly served upon the pre-emptor, and the purchased land has already been mutated in her name vide Mutation Case No.434/75-76 on 15.09.1975 and in the mutation proceeding, notice was also served upon the pre-emptor. Before sale, the vendor pro-posed to sell the case land to the pre-emptor, but he refused to purchase for want of money. The pre-emptor's sisters have also right and title upon the case land and she purchased their share. Since S.A. and R.S. records were wrongly prepared, a suit being Other Class Suit No.477 of 1978 was instituted for cancellation of the records which is still pending in the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Rajshahi and the pre-emption case suffered from defect of non-joinder of necessary parties, and the pre-emptor is not entitled to get any relief as prayed for. 

4. After hearing the parties and considering the materials on record, the Senior Assistant Judge, Rajshahi Sadar, Rajshahi, allowed the pre-emption application by his order dated 30.04.2002. 

5. Being aggrieved by the said order, the pre-emptee preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.24 of 2002 before the District Judge, Rajshahi, which was eventually transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, Second Court, Rajshahi, who after hearing, dismissed the appeal by his judgment and order dated 09.02.2003. 

6. Against the said judgment and order of the appellate Court, the preemptor filed Civil Revision No.2083 of 2003 before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule, which was discharged by the impugned judgment and order. 

7. Thus, the heirs of the pre-emptor as appellants preferred this appeal upon get-ting leave. 

8. Mr. Asaduzzaman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division erred in holding that Miscellaneous Case No.87 of 1978 is barred by limitation inasmuch as the pre-emptor having known about the transfer of the case land filed Preemption Case No.113 of 1975 within the stipulated time limit, but respondent No.1 raised an objection in the said pre-emption case that the case is premature; in view of the fact that the transfer deed had not been registered under section 60 of the Registration Act; the said pre-emption case was dis-missed by the Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi on that sole ground and, therefore, after the transfer deed had been registered on 17.12.1977, the pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No.87 of 1978 after having obtained the certified copy thereof on 03.02.1978 and, as such, there is no scope to say that the pre-emption case is barred by limitation. He further submits that the High Court Division com-mitted an error of law in holding that the pre-emptor refused to purchase the case land for want of money and waives his right of pre-emption inasmuch as it is settled principle of law that the right of pre-emption being a statutory right, the pre-emptor's failure to procure money to purchase the land cannot take away his right of pre-emption if he can come up within time. He lastly submits that the High Court Division erred in not holding that the mutation of the case land in the name of respondent No.1-purchaser does not constitute a bar for the exercise of the right of pre-emption by the pre-emptor inasmuch as admittedly the mutation proceedings had been initiated by respondent No.1 during pendency of the previous pre-emption case filed by the predecessor of the petitioners and as such, respondent No 1 's dealing with the disputed property resulting in sub-division of the holding is hit by the doctrine of lis pendens. 

9. Mr. Abul Kalam Chowdhury, learned Advocate, appearing for respondent No. 1 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He further submits that the appellate Court as the last Court of fact correctly found that before transferring the case land, the vendors offered the same to the appellants' predecessor who refused to purchase for want of money and as such, he or his successors' right of preemption has been waived. He further submits that the appellate Court correctly found that the preemption proceeding is barred by limitation. Previously regarding the same transfer a preemption proceeding was admittedly initiated which was rejected on the reason of immaturity as claimed by the pre-emptor. The instant proceeding for preemption was instituted about after 3(three) years and as such, the appellate Court rightly found that the instant proceeding is barred by limitation. The plea of immaturity as grounded for rejection as claimed by the pre-emptor does not deserve any consideration since the provision of section 60 of the Registration Act does not bear any effect in respect of pre-emption under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural and Tenancy Act as the pre-emptor is a notified co-sharer. 

10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record. 

11. The opposite party (pre-emptee) has come with an allegation that the sale notice was sent to the pre-emptor in time and after serving notice, the case was not filed within 4(four) months for which the suit barred by limitation. On the other hand, the preemptor stated that he filed the suit within 4(four) months after having the knowledge disputed transfer, but the case was disposed of by the trial Court as pre-mature having exhibited the volume of the transfer. The pre-emptor after having registered the case kabala in volume filed the case within due time. There was no proof of having received the notice by the pre-emptor. The present Miscellaneous Case being No.87 of 1978 has been filed on 16.03.1978 and the case kabala has been registered on 17.12.1977 on completion of section 60 of the Registration Act. Thus, the case is suit was filed within limit of time. This case was not defect of parties since all the recorded tenants were being impleaded as parties in this case. The pre-emptor is the co-sharer in the case jute and the defendant is a stranger in the jute. 

12. The appellate Court below found that the case kabala No.30810 was executed on 11.06.1975 and presented for registration on 12.6.1975. Earlier the pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case being No.113 of 1975 for getting the case land pre-empted. This case was dismissed on 24.02.1976 since the same was pre-matured one. It appears that Miscellaneous Case No.113 of 1975 was filed within 12.06.1975. Admittedly, that Miscellaneous Case was dismissed on 24.02.1976 and the deed was registered on 17.12.1977 after completion of provision of section 60 of the Registration Act. It appears that opposite party No.1 paid rent having mutated the suit land. Opposite party No.1 exhibited his Mutation Case No.434/IX1/75-76 dated 15.09.1975 (exhibit-Kha). Ferdousur Rahman while deposing as PW1 on behalf of the petitioner, stated in his cross-examination that opposite party No.1 had been paying rent for 25/26 years. Misc. Case No.113 of 1975 was dismissed having not been written down in registered volume. Opposite party No.1 has not been that since the jama separation order was passed by proper authority, so, opposite party No.1 stopped paying rent and 12 receipts was produced (exhibits-Ga-Gal 1), but the petitioner did not pay any rent. 

13. Admittedly, the S.A. and the R.S. records in respect of the case land were duly prepared in the names of Bazlur Rahman and Fazlur Rahman. Thus, it is enough to implead the heirs of the aforesaid two brothers in this case. Hence, the trial Court is justified in holding that the heirs of the sisters of those two recorded tenants are unnecessary parties in the case. 

14. It is revealed from the record that the pre-emptor earlier filed a case seeking the pre-emption, but the trial Court rejected such pre-emption application on the ground of pre-maturity since the case kabala was not registered and thereby entered in volume book as per provision of section 60 of the Registration Act. It is further revealed that the pre-emptor filed the instant case after long three years of such rejection claiming that the case kabala has been registered as per provision of section 60 of the aforesaid Act. It was wise on part of the trial Court to pass an order of stay of the earlier case instead of rejecting the same. However, the trial Court arrived' at a decision that the afore-said rejection of the earlier case will be counted no bar under Order II, rule-2 of the Code of Civil Procedure nor the principle of res—judicata. The revisional Court including the Court of Appeal below reversed the aforesaid finding of the trial Court on holding that the pre-emptor has got no scope to file the instant case since he has lost his right of pre-emption by filing earlier one. We have considered such legal aspect of the case and are of the opinion that the revisional Court and the Court of appeal failed to appreciate aforementioned legal point in view of the fact that earlier Miscellaneous Case was premature since no cause of action arose for filing the Miscellaneous Pre-emption Case due to non-registration of case kabala. Hence filing of case at that time was a futile exercise. Before registration of case kabala on completion of section 60 of the Registration Act, no cause of action had arisen. But pre-emptor has filed the present case after registration of the case kabala which appears to be a fit case and there is no bar to file a fresh one after dismissal of previous case. Thus, it appears to us that the trial Court appears to be very much justified in deciding this legal issue. 

15. It is the definite case of the pre-emptee that he requested the preemptor to purchase the land before executing the present case kabala, but the pre-emptor refused such offer on the ground of his financial inability and as such, the pre-emptor waived and acquiesced his right of preemption. The trial Court on scrutinizing the evidence on record in this respect has arrived at a decision that the pre-emption right is a legal right accrued in favour of the pre-emptor which cannot be denied on basis of the flimsy ground of waiver and acquiescence. In deciding such factor, the trial Court has observed that opposite party No.1 (opposite party witness No.1.) was not present at the time of such proposal as has been revealed from his cross-examination. It has been further observed by the trial Court that all other opposite party witnesses have made contradictory and inconsistent statements in respect of offering such proposal which makes the same unworthy of trust. In this regard the trial Court observed in the following verbatim:- 
“১নং প্রতিপক্ষ তাহার আপত্তিতে উল-খ করেন যে, দরখাস্তকারীর নালিশী সম্পত্তি ক্রয়ের বিষয় প্রস্তাব দেওয়া হইলে তিনি নিতে অস্বীকার করেন। ফলে তিনি তাহার দাবী পরিত্যাগ করায় নালিশী সম্পত্তি তিনি অগ্রক্রয় মূলে পাইবার অধিকারী নন উক্ত বিষয় প্রমানের ভার ১নং পতিপক্ষের উপর । দেখা যাক উক্ত বিষয় তিনি কতটুকু প্রমান সক্ষম হইয়াছেন। ১নং প্রতিপক্ষের পক্ষে ও. পি. ডবি-উ-১ তাহার জবানবন্দীতে বলেন যে, সায়েলের কাছে বিক্রয়ের প্রস্তাব দিলে তিনি খরিদের অস্বীকৃতি জানান, বলেন যে, তার কাছে টাকা নাই। জেরা কালে ও. পি.ডবি-উ-১ বলেন যে, ফজলারের বাড়ীতে তার ভাতিজারা ক্রয়ের প্রস্তাব দিয়েছিল। কয়টার সময় প্রস্তাব দেয় বলতে পারবো না। তখন আমি উপস্থিত ছিলাম না । সুতরাং দেখা যাচ্ছে যে, ও. পি. ডবি-উ-১ একজন শোনা সাক্ষী । ক্রয়ের প্রস্তাব বিষয় প্রত্যক্ষ কোন সাক্ষী নন। ও. পি. ডবি-উ-২ শামসুদ্দিন আহমেদ তার জবানবন্দীতে বলেন, তিনি রেজিস্ট্রী অফিসে গিয়েছিলেন দলিলের দাতারা তাদের চাচা ফজলারকে কিনতে বলেছি তিনি কিনতে বলেছিল, তিনি কিনতে পারবেন না মর্মে জানিয়েছিলেন । তিনি জনাববন্দীতে আরও উলে-খ করেন যে, ফজলার তার বাড়ীতে আসলে তিনি নালিশী জমি ক্রয়ের বিষয় ফজলারকে বলেন ফজলার এর টাকা নাই মর্মে নিতে অস্বীকার করেছিল। জেরা কালে তিনি বলেন যে, ফজলার রহমানের বাড়ীতে ২-৮নং প্রতিপক্ষ তার সামনে নালিশী সম্পত্তি খাজনারকে খরিদের প্রস্তাব দেয়নি। সুতরাং দেখা যাচ্ছে যে, তিনিও নালিশী অস্বীকৃতির ঘটনার প্রত্যক্ষ সাক্ষী নন।

ও. পি. ডবি-উ-৩ মোঃ নকীর উদ্দিন জবানবন্দীতে বলেন যে, নালিশী সম্পত্তি রেজিন্ত্রীর দিন খাজনার ও তার ভাতিজা রহমান পুকুর দেখিতেছিল। তিনি তার চাচা নিতে পারতেন মর্মে বিশ্বাস করাতে সে বলেছিল তার চাচার টাকা নাই। জেরা কালে তিনি বলেন যে, রেজিস্ত্রীর ১ দিন আগে আবদুর রহমান ও ফজলারের সংগে কার্ষ্য করা হয় সকাল ৯ টায়। অত্র সাক্ষীর সাক্ষ্য পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, তার নিজের সাক্ষ্যই পরস্পর বিরোধী । একবার তিনি বলেন রেজিস্ত্রীর আগের দিন কার্য্য হওয়ার বিষয় আরেকবার বলেন রেজিন্ত্রীর দিন কথা হবার বিষয়। তার সাক্ষ্যে দরখাস্তকারীর সুনির্দিষ্ট ২-৮নং প্রতিপক্ষের প্রস্তাব অস্বীকৃতির বিষয়টি প্রমান হয় না।

ও. পি. ডবি-উ-৪ মোঃ ইসতিয়াক আহমেদ তার সাক্ষ্যে বলেন যে, নকির উদ্দিন, পচা ডাক্তার, আবদুর রহমান ২৫/২৬ বসর আগে সকাল ৯/৯:৩০ টার দিকে আলাপ করে। সরিক সাহেব নালিশী জমি কেন কিন্ত কিনে দেন না মর্মে আবদুর রহমানকে জিজ্ঞাসা করেছিল। জেরা কালে তিনি উক্ত কথাবার্তার সন, মাস, তারিখ বলতে পারবেন না মর্মে জানান এবং তার উপস্থিতিতে কথা হয় মর্মে বলেন। ও. পি. ডবি-উ-৪ এর সাক্ষ্যের বর্ণনার সাথে অন্যান্য সাক্ষীর সাক্ষ্যের বর্ণনার যথেষ্ট বৈসাদৃশ্য আছে মর্মে পরিলক্ষিত হয়। অন্য যে কোন সাক্ষী নালিশী বিক্রয়ের কথা বার্তার সময় ও. পি. ডবি-উ-৪ দিন মর্মে সাক্ষ্য প্রদান করেন নাই । উপরক্ত তার সাক্ষ্যে পচা ডাক্তার এর সাথে আবদুর রহমানের কথা হবার বিষয় এবং চাচা ডাক্তারের নালিশী সম্পত্তি কিনতে অস্বীকৃতির বিষয় আসে নাই।

উপরোক্ত সাক্ষী সমূহের সাক্ষ্য পর্যালণচনায় দেখা যায় যে, প্রতিপক্ষ নালিশী সম্পত্তির দাবী দরখাস্ত কারী পরিত্যাগ করেছিল মর্মে দাবী করিলেও তার লিখিত কোন প্রমান যেমন আদালতে হাজির করিতে পারেন নাই সেই সাথে মৌখিক সাক্ষ্য দ্বারাও সুনির্দিষ্ট ভাবে সেরূপ কোন ঘটনা তারা প্রমান করতে পারেন নাই, প্রত্যেক সাক্ষীর সাক্ষ্যই ভাসা ভাসা । উক্ত সাক্ষী দ্বারা দরখাস্তকারীর দাবী পরিত্যাগের বিষয় সন্দেহাতীতভাবে প্রমান হয় না। প্রিয়েমশান অধিকার একটি আইনগত অধিকার । এই অধিকারকে ওপেন ওয়েভার একুইসেন্স এর হালকা অভিযোগ দিয়ে নষ্ট করা যায় না যদি না সেরূপ অভিযোগের সুনির্দিষ্ট ভিত্তি থাকে । সুতরাং বলা যায় যে, প্রতিপক্ষ দরখাস্তকারীর দাবী পরিত্যাগের বিষয় প্রমান করিতে সক্ষম হন নাই বিধায় এই কারনে তিনি দরখাস্তকারীকে প্রিয়েমশানের অধিকার হইতে বঞ্চিত করার হকদার নন ।”

16. We have also gone through those testimonies of the OPWs and shifting of evidence as has been done by the trial Court in above quoted observation which appears to be proper and acceptable. Thus, we are inclined to support such observation and decision. We have also gone through the evidence on record which is very much consistent with aforementioned observation of the trial Court. We have meticulously examined the finding and decisions of the Court of appeal below as well as revisional Court along with the facts and circumstances in the case and found that the finding of the trial Court is much acceptable and logical than that of others. 

17. We have no hesitation in holding that the revisional Court as well as the Court of appeal has overlooked all those evidence on record which is nothing but sheer misreading, miss-appreciation and non-consideration of legal evidence. 

18. Having considered those facts, circumstances and evidence on record, we have no option but to interfere with the impugned judgment along with the judgment of the Court of appeal below. 

19. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed, without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order along with the judgment and order of the appellate Court below is hereby set aside. The judgment and order of the trial Court is hereby restored. 

End.
